subject: Turning an alcove into a workspace
hook: Alcove desks go wrong in the same five ways. Here's how to avoid each one.
ig:
Alcove desks go wrong in the same five ways. Here's how to avoid each one.

An alcove beside a chimney breast is one of the best spots for a small home office. It's tucked away, it uses dead space, and it can be closed off visually at the end of the day. But it's also easy to get wrong.

1. Assuming both alcoves match. They almost never do.
2. Forgetting cables. Three walls means nowhere for a lead to go without a planned route.
3. Drawers under the desk. In a narrow alcove they steal your legroom.
4. Shelves at head height. You'll hit it every time you stand up.
5. No light. Alcoves are shady; plan a lamp socket or task light.

Get these right and a fitted alcove desk can be a properly comfortable place to work.

Got an alcove that's become a dumping ground? It could be your new home office.

Alcoves beside a chimney breast make brilliant little workspaces, but there are a few classic mistakes: assuming both alcoves are the same size, forgetting where the cables will go, filling the legroom with drawers, and putting a shelf right where your head will be.

We've listed all five in this carousel. If you're thinking about working from a corner of the living room or spare room, have a flick through first.

on_asset: S1: Alcove desk mistakes | Five things to get right first time | S2: Assuming both alcoves match — Alcoves either side of a chimney breast are rarely identical. Measure each one separately, at several heights. | S3: Forgetting the cables — With walls on three sides, there's nowhere for a cable to escape. Plan a grommet and a route to the socket. | S4: Drawers where your knees go — A drawer pedestal eats legroom in a narrow alcove. Keep the knee space clear and put storage above or to one side. | S5: Shelves at head height — A shelf you bump into every time you stand up gets removed. Set it high enough to clear you. | S6: Ignoring the light — Alcoves can be dark.
